---

  This document summarizes the interagency trawl program results from August of `r this_year`, combining Ontario MNR and Ohio DOW trawl catches to obtain Western Basin estimates of fish per hectare. These should be considered preliminary data and **should not be shared with the public**. 
  
  
### Methods 
  Briefly, trawl catches are transformed to catch per hectare using trawl distance and SCANMAR-derived, vessel-specific wing widths. Fishing Power Corrections are applied to catches from the ODNR R/V *Explorer* (1988–2002) and *Explorer* (2003–present; same name, different vessel) to correct those vessels' fishing power to the OMNR R/V *Keenosay* (Tyson et al. 2006). Catch-per-hectare is then extrapolated up to country- and depth-specific strata area and then divided by the total basin area to yield a basinwide abundance estimate (in fish per hectare).

## Trawl Effort
![](figures/maps/2026 effort map.png)

Ontario and Ohio combined to attempt `r effort_summary$trawl_sites` trawl sites in August `r this_year`, of which `r effort_summary$low_do_sites` site was removed due to hypoxia (<2.0 mg/L; blue points) and `r effort_summary$bad_trawl_sites` were removed due to other issues. In total, `r effort_summary$good_trawl_sites` sites were used in this year's index calculations.

\newpage

## Walleye Indices

### Young-of-year index
![Young-of-year Walleye catch per hectare, Western Basin Lake Erie](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 334_1.png)
The Western Basin YOY Walleye index in `r this_year` was again high (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "334_1")]` fish/ha) compared to the overall time series. This is the `r ranks$rank[which(ranks$spp_agegroup == "334_1")]` greatest year class since 1988.

### Young-of-year Walleye Map
![](figures/maps/percid indices/age-0 334 map.png)

Catches of age-0 Walleye were concentrated in eastern Ontario waters and between the islands in Ohio waters.

### Yearling Walleye Index
![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 334_2.png)

The yearling Walleye index was high (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "334_2")]` fish/ha) compared to recent years and to the overall time series, the largest since 2020. This is the `r ranks$rank[which(ranks$spp_agegroup == "334_2")]` greatest yearling year class since 1988.
\newpage

## Yellow Perch Indices

### Young-of-year index
![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 331_1.png)

The Western Basin YOY Yellow Perch index in `r this_year` was high (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "331_1")]` fish/ha) compared to the time series and was the greatest since 2020. This is the `r ranks$rank[which(ranks$spp_agegroup == "331_1")]` greatest year class since 1988.

### Young-of-year Yellow Perch Map
![](figures/maps/percid indices/age-0 331 map.png)

Catches of age-0 Yellow Perch were concentrated in Ontario waters, near Pigeon Bay (west of Point Pelee) and west of Pelee Island. Ohio catches were greatest near the Detroit River plume

### Yearling
![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 331_2.png)

The yearling Yellow Perch index was high (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "331_2")]` fish/ha). This is the `r ranks$rank[which(ranks$spp_agegroup == "331_2")]` greatest yearling year class since 1988.

\newpage
## Ohio vs Ontario Percid Index Contribution
![](figures/country contribution/percid index contribution - percentage.png)

Each jurisdiction's relative contribution to the percid indices differed somewhat. Ontario caught substantially more age-0 Yellow Perch and Walleye.



![](figures/country contribution/trend in percid index contribution.png)
Ohio's relative contribution to the interagency index continues to trend down for both species.

\newpage

## Total Forage Index

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance by forage group.png)

Total forage density in `r this_year` was typical of the last few years (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "all_forage")]` fish/ha) and similar to last year. As usual, forage makeup was dominated by spiny-rayed prey (e.g., White Perch, Yellow Perch, and Walleye; `r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "spiny_ray")]` fish/ha). Note that 2021 catches were skewed due to a hypoxia-related outlier catch.

\newpage

## Major Forage Species Indices
### Young-of-year White Perch

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 301_1.png)

YOY White Perch abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "301_1")]` fish/ha) was similar to last year - about half of the ten-year mean abundance (`r abund$ten_year_mean[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "301_1")]` fish/ha).


### Young-of-year Gizzard Shad

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 63_1.png)

YOY Gizzard Shad abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "63_1")]` fish/ha) was average compared to recent years but low compared to the time series;  abundance was down compared to the ten-year mean (`r abund$ten_year_mean[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "63_1")]` fish/ha).

\newpage

### Young-of-year Emerald Shiner

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 196_1.png)

YOY Emerald Shiner abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "196_1")]` fish/ha) remained minimal in `r this_year`, continuing a trend of low abundance for this historically-important forage fish. Shiner abundance is likely to remain low while the adult Walleye population is large (Knight and Vondracek 1993).

### Adult Emerald Shiner

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 196_3.png)

Adult (ages-1+) Emerald Shiner abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "196_3")]` fish/ha) also remained minimal, continuing a trend of low abundance.

\newpage

### Round Goby

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 366_5.png)

Round Goby abundance across all ages (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "366_5")]` fish/ha) has been fairly stable for five years, lower than the 10 year mean (`r abund$ten_year_mean[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "366_5")]` fish/ha).

\newpage

## Other Catches of Note
### Young-of-year White Bass

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 302_1.png)

YOY White Bass abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "302_1")]` fish/ha) fell from last year's recent high.

### Young-of-year Freshwater Drum

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 371_1.png)

YOY Freshwater Drum abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "371_1")]` fish/ha) was the largest since 2021.

### Young-of-year Spottail Shiner

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 201_1.png)

YOY Spottail Shiner were also found in high abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "201_1")]` fish/ha), the greatest since 2005.

### Adult Spottail Shiner

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 201_3.png)

Adult Spottail Shiner abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "201_3")]` fish/ha) was comparable to recent years.

### Adult Silver Chub

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 191_3.png)

Adult Silver Chub abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "191_1")]` fish/ha) was again high, after reaching the largest abundance in survey history last year (since 1988).
